stories.title: Tether posts $1.5 billion Q2 profit as reserve buffer halves
stories.summary: Tether reported $1.5 billion in operating profit for the second quarter, but its excess reserve cushion fell by more than $4 billion over the same period, roughly halving in 90 days. Multiple outlets note the headline profit figure masks a larger hit to the buffer that backs USDT.
stories.whyItMatters: Tether's reserve adequacy underpins confidence in the largest stablecoin, so a rapidly shrinking safety margin matters for anyone relying on USDT liquidity or stability.
whatToWatch: Whether Tether's next attestation shows the reserve buffer stabilizing or continuing to shrink
Any regulatory or market reaction to the reserve decline
questions: What specifically drove the $4 billion drop in excess reserves?
Is the shrinking buffer a one-off or a trend?

stories.title: Coinbase shares slip on Q2 results despite prediction-market growth
stories.summary: Coinbase's stock fell after its Q2 earnings even though prediction markets on the platform reportedly doubled and the company posted record trading market share. The mixed reaction suggests investors focused on other parts of the report.
stories.whyItMatters: Coinbase is a bellwether for U.S. crypto trading activity and investor sentiment toward listed crypto companies.
whatToWatch: Follow-up commentary from Coinbase management on what weighed on the stock
Growth trajectory of prediction markets on the platform
questions: What specifically disappointed investors if trading share and prediction markets grew?

stories.title: Bank of Italy: stablecoins don't consistently cut remittance costs
stories.summary: New research from the Bank of Italy found that stablecoins do not offer a consistent cost advantage over traditional channels for remittances, challenging a common pitch for crypto payment rails.
stories.whyItMatters: Cheaper cross-border payments is one of the main real-world use cases claimed for stablecoins, so central-bank research questioning that claim could shape policy and adoption debates.
whatToWatch: Whether other central banks publish similar comparative studies
Industry response from stablecoin issuers
questions: What specific corridors or use cases were tested in the study?

stories.title: Bitcoin mining difficulty drops 14% from yearly high as revenues sag
stories.summary: Bitcoin's mining difficulty has fallen 14% from this year's peak as shrinking mining revenues push some operators to pivot their business models. The move comes as bitcoin and ether prices softened even as equities rallied and the broader crypto market headed for its best month in a year.
stories.whyItMatters: Falling difficulty and revenue pressure signal stress in the mining sector, which affects network security economics and miner stock valuations.
whatToWatch: Further difficulty adjustments in coming weeks
Miner pivots toward AI/data-center hosting or other revenue lines
questions: Which specific operators are pivoting, and to what business lines?

stories.title: Solana Foundation's new security chief flags AI-driven crypto scams
stories.summary: The Solana Foundation's newly appointed CISO warned that artificial intelligence is making crypto scams more convincing, an issue likely to be a focus for the foundation's security efforts going forward.
stories.whyItMatters: AI-enhanced phishing and social-engineering scams pose growing risk to retail crypto users and could increase losses across the ecosystem.
whatToWatch: Any concrete security measures the Solana Foundation rolls out in response
questions: What specific scam tactics is the CISO most concerned about?

stories.title: SEC to review Nasdaq's bitcoin options approval after CME objection
stories.summary: The SEC will review its approval of Nasdaq-listed bitcoin options after CME challenged the decision, putting the product's status in question while regulators reconsider.
stories.whyItMatters: The outcome could affect competition between exchanges for regulated bitcoin derivatives and shape how new crypto products get approved.
whatToWatch: SEC's review timeline and decision
CME's next steps if the review doesn't go its way
questions: What specific grounds did CME cite in its challenge?

stories.title: Coldcard hardware wallet exploit tied to at least $38 million in losses
stories.summary: An exploit affecting Coldcard hardware wallets has been linked to at least $38 million in losses so far, according to CoinDesk, raising questions about self-custody security. The incident may push some investors toward custodial options like ETFs instead of holding keys themselves.
stories.whyItMatters: Self-custody is a core crypto value proposition; a high-profile hardware wallet exploit could shift more capital toward regulated, custodial products.
whatToWatch: Whether the loss figure grows as more victims come forward
Coldcard's response and any patch or recall
questions: What was the actual vulnerability exploited?
Are other hardware wallet brands affected by similar flaws?

stories.title: Institutional bitcoin holders reportedly sitting on $16.3 billion in unrealized losses
stories.summary: An analysis suggests Wall Street institutions are collectively holding roughly $16.3 billion in unrealized bitcoin losses, with an August 14 disclosure deadline (likely tied to 13F filings) expected to reveal which institutions have been reducing positions.
stories.whyItMatters: 13F-style disclosures give a rare window into institutional conviction (or capitulation) on bitcoin ETFs and holdings.
whatToWatch: August 14 disclosure deadline and resulting filings
Whether major holders reduce or add to positions
questions: How was the $16.3 billion loss figure calculated, and over what price basis?

stories.title: New York sues Kalshi, alleging illegal gambling operation
stories.summary: New York has sued prediction-market platform Kalshi, alleging it runs an illegal gambling operation rather than a legitimate derivatives exchange. Reports indicate the state is seeking damages as large as $36 billion.
stories.whyItMatters: The case is a major test of whether federally-regulated prediction markets can operate in states with gambling restrictions, with implications for the fast-growing prediction-market sector including crypto-adjacent platforms.
whatToWatch: Kalshi's legal response and any injunction requests
Whether other states follow New York's lead
questions: How does this interact with Kalshi's federal CFTC registration?
Will the case affect crypto-linked prediction markets like those Coinbase is expanding?

stories.title: Coinbase's diversification push still posted a $359 million loss
stories.summary: Despite roughly five years spent building businesses beyond core bitcoin/crypto trading, Coinbase reportedly posted a $359 million loss in the period covered, according to CryptoSlate's analysis of its results.
stories.whyItMatters: The figure raises questions about how effectively Coinbase's diversification strategy is offsetting the cyclicality of trading revenue.
whatToWatch: Coinbase's next earnings for signs of improvement in diversified revenue lines
questions: Which specific business lines drove the $359 million loss?

stories.title: Circle wins New York trust charter for a subsidiary

stories.whyItMatters: A trust charter gives Circle a more regulated footing in a major financial hub, potentially strengthening USDC's standing versus rivals amid tightening stablecoin oversight.
whatToWatch: How Circle uses the charter operationally
Whether competitors like Tether pursue similar charters
questions: What specific powers does the New York trust charter grant the subsidiary?

stories.whyItMatters: ETF flow trends remain one of the clearest signals of institutional demand for bitcoin exposure.
whatToWatch: August ETF flow data for signs of whether the late-July selling continues
questions: Which specific funds drove the late-month outflows?
